comparisons.interpretation: Both support practical zoning/use flexibility to help businesses operate during the pandemic, rather than opposite positions inferred from endorsement labels.

Both support civilian police review. Fenwick explicitly calls for disciplinary authority; Mulvihill discusses a review panel and state-granted subpoena power. The shared goal does not establish identical institutional powers.

Fenwick foregrounds changing the policing/incarceration spending emphasis toward prevention; Mulvihill foregrounds warrant restrictions, auditing, training and oversight. A categorical Mulvihill opposition to prevention or a precise budget difference is not invented.

Fenwick stresses anti-displacement investment and implementing neighborhood plans; Mulvihill stresses business-corridor renewal, aging-in-place housing and connectivity. Both discuss neighborhood quality of life with different priorities.
